atlas-de.0148: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Frankfurt 29th in the world (down 14 places) and ninth among Western European centres, behind London, Zurich, Geneva, Luxembourg, Lugano, Paris, Copenhagen and Amsterdam; Berlin is 45th, Munich 58th (up 15) and Hamburg 84th, and Stuttgart is an associate centre.
atlas-de.0149: Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Munich, Wolfsburg and Ludwigshafen are among the ten districts and cities with the highest median monthly pay of full-time employees in Germany on 31 December 2024; the top is Ingolstadt at €5,855, against a national median of €4,013.
atlas-de.0150: Frankfurt am Main has 761,090 jobs (2023), 259,390 of them (34%) in finance and insurance, real estate and professional and business services, and only 39,890 in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0151: Deutsche Börse Group’s headquarters is in Eschborn, just outside Frankfurt’s city limits, with more than 3,100 employees; the Frankfurt Stock Exchange trading hall is in the Alte Börse in the city centre.
atlas-de.0152: Frankfurt Airport City employs approximately 80,000 people at some 500 companies and organisations on site, one of Germany’s largest job complexes at a single location.
atlas-de.0153: Munich city has 1,203,650 jobs (2023): 340,320 in finance and insurance, real estate and professional and business services, 327,110 in trade, transport, hospitality and information and communication, and 113,320 in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0154: Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts the value of Munich’s start-up ecosystem at $71 billion (Europe’s average $14.3 billion, the world’s $25 billion), with $2.3 billion of seed and Series A funding and $10 billion of exits in 2021–2025.
atlas-de.0155: Startup Genome’s 2026 report ranks Berlin 22nd among the world’s start-up ecosystems and third in Europe (also third in Europe for talent and for its AI-native cluster), with an ecosystem value of $89.5 billion.
atlas-de.0156: Berlin has 2,190,900 jobs (2023), 170,560 of them in information and communication, 43,450 in finance and insurance and 432,460 in professional, scientific, technical and administrative services.
atlas-de.0157: Hamburg has 1,348,210 jobs (2023), 87,670 of them in information and communication, 45,240 in finance and insurance and 109,100 in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0158: In 2024 Hamburg handled 97.0 million tonnes of goods, the third-busiest port in the EU after Rotterdam (397.3 million) and Antwerp-Bruges (244.2 million).
atlas-de.0159: Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts the value of Hamburg’s start-up ecosystem at $6 billion, with $962 million of seed and Series A funding in H2 2023–2025.
atlas-de.0160: Stuttgart city has 548,450 jobs (2023), 77,320 of them (14%) in manufacturing and 140,560 in finance and insurance, real estate and professional and business services.
atlas-de.0161: Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts the value of Stuttgart’s start-up ecosystem at $6 billion, with $293 million of seed and Series A funding in H2 2023–2025.
atlas-de.0162: Mannheim city has 249,430 jobs (2023), 41,640 of them in manufacturing; Heidelberg has 129,740 and the Rhein-Neckar district 247,100.
atlas-de.0163: BASF’s Ludwigshafen site, the origin of its Verbund system, has around 33,000 employees, 125 production plants and calls itself the largest integrated chemical complex in the world.
atlas-de.0164: SAP reports 110,000 employees from 157-plus countries, total revenue of €36.8 billion (non-IFRS) in 2025 and 100-plus development locations.
atlas-de.0165: Düsseldorf city has 576,590 jobs (2023), 175,900 of them (31%) in finance and insurance, real estate and professional and business services and 167,350 in trade, transport, hospitality and information and communication.
atlas-de.0166: Rheinmetall AG has its head office in Düsseldorf (Rheinmetall Platz 1) and says it employs around 34,000 people at 161 offices and production sites in more than 30 countries (status July 2026, continuing operations).
atlas-de.0167: More than 5,300 people work at Henkel’s headquarters site in Düsseldorf-Holthausen, which covers more than 1.42 million square metres; Henkel as a whole has about 50,000 employees worldwide, more than 80% of them outside Germany.
atlas-de.0168: Wolfsburg has 131,830 jobs (2023), 71,080 of them (54%) in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0169: The Wolfsburg plant has approximately 70,000 employees, built 490,000 vehicles in 2023 and is the headquarters of Volkswagen Passenger Cars.
atlas-de.0170: Nuremberg city has 406,850 jobs (2023); the neighbouring district of Erlangen-Höchstadt, where Herzogenaurach lies, has 68,010, of them 18,180 in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0171: DATEV eG, the software and IT services cooperative for tax advisers, accountants and companies, has its seat at Paumgartnerstraße in Nuremberg and says more than 9,000 people work for it, with €1.51 billion of revenue in 2024.
atlas-de.0172: The central office of the Federal Employment Agency is at Regensburger Straße 104 in Nuremberg, a 17-storey building where the divisions set the agency’s labour-market programmes, finances and personnel policy.
atlas-de.0173: Trade press reporting Infineon’s announcement says the company opened its Smart Power Fab in Dresden in July 2026, several months ahead of schedule: an investment of five billion euros, the largest in Infineon’s history, creating 1,000 new direct jobs and doubling its manufacturing capacity at the Dresden site.
atlas-de.0174: Dresden city has 350,030 jobs (2023), 41,710 of them in industry (mining, manufacturing, energy and water) including 36,920 in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0175: More than 50 German insurers and reinsurers have their headquarters in Cologne, which Cologne’s economic development calls the second-largest German insurance location, with about 24,000 employees subject to social insurance.
atlas-de.0176: Cologne had 631,907 employees subject to social insurance at its workplaces in 2025, 553,626 of them in services and 78,281 in production.
atlas-de.0177: Essen has 350,160 jobs (2023) and Dortmund 346,380; in Essen 93,570 are in finance and insurance, real estate and professional and business services.
atlas-de.0178: RWE AG gives its address as RWE Platz 1, Essen, where it is registered (district court Essen).
atlas-de.0179: thyssenkrupp AG gives its address as thyssenkrupp Allee 1, Essen, with registered offices in Duisburg and Essen.
atlas-de.0180: Brenntag’s head office is at Messeallee 11 in Essen.
atlas-de.0181: The Hanover region has 703,250 jobs (2023), 74,620 of them in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0182: Continental’s headquarters is at Continental-Plaza 1 in Hanover; its new campus was inaugurated in December 2023 for about 2,400 employees from corporate functions and the Tires and ContiTech divisions.
atlas-de.0183: Talanx describes itself as based in Hannover and reports insurance revenue of €48,994 million for 2025.
atlas-de.0184: Leipzig city has 365,780 jobs (2023), 28,180 of them in manufacturing and 93,610 in finance and insurance, real estate and professional and business services.

atlas-de.0186: More than 4,600 people work at Porsche Leipzig, which builds around 550 Macan and Panamera models a day and is the brand’s centre of excellence for electromobility.
atlas-de.0187: The Karlsruhe Institute of Technology reports 23,083 students, 10,131 employees, 424 professors and 68 new spin-offs and start-ups in 2025.
atlas-de.0188: Karlsruhe city has 240,790 jobs (2023), 71,910 of them in trade, transport, hospitality and information and communication and 52,850 in finance and insurance, real estate and professional and business services.
atlas-de.0189: CyberForum, the network of Karlsruhe’s IT cluster, has about 1,200 member companies that together account for around 30,000 jobs, and runs a federally recognised digital hub for cybersecurity.
atlas-de.0190: IONOS Group, the cloud infrastructure and web hosting company, gives Karlsruhe as its address.
atlas-de.0191: Deutsche Telekom’s group headquarters is at Friedrich-Ebert-Allee 140 in Bonn; the group has around 200,000 employees worldwide (31 December 2025) and more than 12,000 people in Bonn and the surrounding region work for it, making it Bonn’s largest employer.
atlas-de.0192: Bonn has 27 United Nations institutions on its UN Campus, with a staff of almost a thousand.
atlas-de.0193: Bonn city has 269,690 jobs (2023), 135,860 of them (50%) in public administration, education, health, arts and other services, and only 8,510 in manufacturing.
atlas-de.0194: Germany hires its graduates from people it already knows. When a firm approves budget for juniors, the first places go to its own working students (Werkstudenten), then to its interns and thesis students, and only then to outside applicants.
atlas-de.0195: A cold application from abroad competes for what is left.
atlas-de.0197: A paid part-time job of up to 20 hours a week during term, held while enrolled at a German university, often for a year or more in the same team. It is the main bridge into a first contract in software, consulting, finance functions and industry.
atlas-de.0198: Not every working student is kept: in StepStone’s data for 2017 about a third were taken on permanently, against half of interns.
atlas-de.0199: Internship (Praktikum) and the thesis in a company
atlas-de.0200: A three-to-six-month internship, or a master’s thesis written inside a company (Abschlussarbeit im Unternehmen), works as a long trial. In a 2022 survey of more than 500 HR managers, personality, practical experience and the thesis topic and grade ranked above the name of the school.
atlas-de.0201: Strategy consulting is the clearest case: BCG takes outstanding interns into its FAST FORWARD programme on their last internship day, with a full-time offer and no further interviews.
atlas-de.0202: Graduate programme or direct entry (Trainee, Direkteinstieg)
atlas-de.0203: Large groups run trainee programmes and post junior jobs openly; this is where outside applicants compete, and it is the part of the market that shrank most after 2022.
atlas-de.0204: Programmes are for recent graduates: BASF takes people with at most 2 years of work experience and Deutsche Bank’s graduate programme at most 12 months, and BASF’s two named programmes require a master’s; Commerzbank takes graduates whose last degree is no more than 18 months old.
